title: The need for legal protection for teachers from parents' immoderate accusations
text:
The suicide of a teacher at Seoi Elementary School was in the news recently. In that case, it was accepted that the teacher died on the job, but the parents were ruled to be innocent, and the case ended with no perpetrator. Although the incident was recognized as an on-the-job death, the investigation concluded that the parents were not accountable, leaving the case unresolved without identifying a perpetrator. This raises the question: can we truly say there is no perpetrator in this case? Teachers are suffering constantly from reckless reports of child abuse and relentless complaints from parents and these lead to teachers’ psychological and physical pain. We should focus on the fact that teachers have no legal protection to be protected despite this challenge. I believe there should be systems and laws to stop imprudent parent's actions and protect teachers.
First, the cases of conflicts between teachers and parents show that there is a need for a system to control the indiscriminate behavior of parents that is a threat to the educational environment. In particular, according to Donghyuk Jeon (2023), there was a case where parents visited the elementary school classroom in class. The parent verbally abused and assaulted the teacher in the presence of all the children and was arrested for one year in prison. Parent-teacher conflict is something that has been going on for a long time, even though it hasn't been brought to the spotlight. This case is one of those cases where the growing conflict and the suffering of teachers became a major issue. This case, which exposed a teacher to direct attack and danger, highlights the lack of physical and psychological protection for teachers. The parent was given a one-year prison sentence for injuring a teacher and emotionally abusing elementary school students. Teachers can only take legal action if they are directly and physically assaulted, and it is difficult for them to defend themselves against false accusations or other complaints that threaten teachers. In one case, a parent secretly recorded a class to prove that his child had been abused and to get evidence. Webtoonist Joo Homin suspected that his son was being abused by a teacher, so he secretly recorded the class by putting a recorder in his son's backpack. According to Lee Jeongha, the National Special Teachers' Union pointed out that the court had accepted the illegal recordings as evidence. Apart from the division of victims and perpetrators, there are often cases where parents' complaints are excessively violent, disruptive, or violate the rights of teachers and children. In this regard, a system to control aggressive complaints and excessive behavior is necessary for educational environments.
Second, The huge amount of complaints and accusations that teachers and schools are facing shows that parents' imprudent actions are threatening the educational environment, and an effective solution is needed. In one case, a parent of an elementary school student claimed child abuse against the principal and filed numerous lawsuits and complaints. Yunsu Ji (2023) states “The parent filed seven lawsuits and complaints, 8 administrative appeals, 29 requests for information disclosure, 24 the National Newspaper, and various other lawsuits and complaints” and “The school district filed a police complaint against the parent for false accusations and defamation, claiming that it caused the school's administrative functions to be paralyzed”. "The pain and psychological anxiety that teachers suffer during police investigations are entirely on their own," said Jaeseok Jeong, president of the Jeonbuk Teachers' Union. This case highlights the difficulties that teachers and schools suffer from unreasonable parental complaints and lawsuits and emphasizes the need to control them. Too many unreasonable complaints not only challenge the work of schools and teachers but also cause psychological distress to teachers who are unable to react to this suffering. There is currently no legal or systemic way to prevent a situation like the one in this case, and no way for teachers to be protected.
Last, the current response of the Office of Education shows the flaw of protecting teachers and preventing false accusations, and the need for effective measures to control false accusations. After the case of Seoi Elementary School, the Office of Education said it would send a school violence investigator to each school, but it does not actually purposely protect teachers and relieve the burden of their responsibility for school violence cases. The action of the Office of Education was not great in preventing a repetition of a situation like this incident because school violence investigators can only help in steps of investigation and it can not control parents' immoderate actions. Although the school violence investigator relieves teachers of the burden of investigating incidents, the conflict between parents and teachers, including the case of Seoi Elementary School, is more about the failure to control unreasonable complaining and the failure to protect teachers than the burden of school violence-related work. According to the teachers' union, there is an example of a teacher being forced to spend nearly two years in court due to the parents' counterclaims. The teachers' union called for a system to prevent false accusations. A teacher in the case of Seoi Elementary School reported receiving repeated calls from parents on her personal phone number. Yoo Chaeyoung stated that many teachers' personal contacts are often used by parents to complain. As such, teachers are not properly protected. The system of school violence investigators created after the case of Seoi Elementary School is not enough to prevent or solve other similar problems. Additional systems need to be created to control unreasonable protests and protect teachers.
Protecting teachers and controlling parents' indiscriminate actions are essential to improving our education system and promoting the development of future generations. To achieve this, governments and Education officials must create thoughtful measures and effective systems. By strengthening regulations to limit reckless complaints, creating communication channels to receive and handle complaints, and making it impossible for teachers to disclose their personal contact information, we can manage and control the mass of complaints and protect teachers and the educational environment. We must work to ensure an educational environment where everyone feels safe and supported. By controlling indiscriminate complaints, we will be able to solve the difficulties of teachers and schools and build a system that can systematically reflect the opinions of parents.

title: How small and medium-sized enterprises can better competitive position against major enterprises: improving working conditions by reducing working hours
text:
The problem of intensifying competition for employment due to concentration in major enterprises is currently receiving a lot of public attention. As a result, small and medium-sized enterprises are experiencing a chronic labor shortage, negatively affecting our economy and society, including the job market. According to a survey by the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, 64.3% of workers prefer major enterprises, which is significantly higher than the 15.7% who prefer small and medium-sized enterprises. As of 2024, the preference for major enterprises and bias for small and medium-sized enterprises still exist, and according to Kwon Hanill, the preference for major enterprises among teenagers and young adults is steadily increasing. It is not only a sign that small and medium-sized enterprises are being pushed out of the competition but also suggests that workers have negative perceptions of small and medium-sized enterprises. One solution to this problem is to reduce working hours. By providing a better working environment for workers, it is expected to make small and medium-sized enterprises more competitive. The intensifying competition for employment due to the concentration of major enterprises comes from the gap in working conditions between major and small and medium-sized enterprises. Major enterprises are creating quality work environments that attract workers and earn their favor. Small and medium-sized enterprises need to be competitive by providing a better working environment, especially when it comes to working hours.
The first step is surveying demand and planning for shorter work hours. Small and medium-sized enterprises need to conduct a demand survey to ask workers about reducing working hours. This helps them understand the needs and desires of their workers, which they can then use to create a plan to reduce working hours appropriately. Based on the results of the survey, set the appropriate amount of adjustment to the working hours. According to “Hankook Economic Daily," in a survey of 1,000 employees over the age of 19, 42.5 percent of workers said they would like to reduce their working hours by four hours. Depending on the industry and the job, the amount of time that workers want to work will vary, but we can assume that many workers would like to reduce their working hours. In the survey, enterprises should find out how much they want to reduce their working hours and what kind of work system they want. Based on the survey results, they will need to set the right amount of adjustment for the working hours for the enterprise.
The second step is to reorganize work processes and reduce working hours. Based on the surveys from earlier, adjust work processes and start reducing working hours. Reducing working hours requires reorganizing work processes. Small and medium-sized enterprises need to reorganize their work processes to increase efficiency and reduce the workload of workers. This will reduce the work intensity of workers and increase their productivity. There are enterprises that have successfully reorganized work and reduced working hours. Enterprises in various industries, such as Nada Digital, Lulu Lab, KTcs, and Kyodong Food, have succeeded in innovative work arrangements. In particular, Gyodong Food designed a work environment that suits the enterprise's situation to secure manpower and operate the workforce effectively (Ministry of Employment and Labor, n.d.). It created a new work process by moving one of the steps of a production system to a new location (Ministry of Employment and Labor, n.d.). The creation of part-time jobs and the new production system created a synergistic effect. In this way, reorganizing work and changing working hours to suit each enterprise can lead to more efficient and effective growth and change.
The third step is financial support for both the company and the worker. In the early days of reducing working hours, enterprises may experience losses and workers may experience reduced earnings, so financial support is needed for both enterprises and workers to minimize the damage from reducing working hours. Government support or tax incentives should help small and medium-sized enterprises implement reduced working hours, and a financial reward system should be set up internally to compensate workers for reduced wages. Presently, the government is implementing the Employment Stability Incentive Program for employers. Since not all enterprises can achieve the same business effectiveness and performance with the same working hours, the government provides support to reduce the burden on enterprises due to the reduction of working hours. It is necessary to further expand this support system so that more employers in various industries can receive government support. It is also needed to ensure that enterprises support their workers so that they can adapt to the reduction in working hours and find a balance in their lives, based on government support and stabilized company performance. It is important to support workers by considering their work performance and salary reduction.
The final step is to regularly evaluate workers' job performance. Regularly monitor and evaluate work performance due to reduced working hours. Check the results and achievements to ensure that productivity does not drop due to reduced working hours and that the changed working hours and work processes are stabilized. This way, the satisfaction of workers and the performance of the company are managed together. KTcs, a company that introduced part-time jobs to reduce working hours and create a flexible work environment, created a new performance evaluation system to identify and reduce performance decline. Since working hours and performance are not always proportional in call center counseling and marketing jobs, KTcs conducted a qualitative evaluation that included the content of counseling, attitudes, and customer responses rather than factors such as the total amount of counseling (Ministry of Employment and Labor, n.d.). The evaluation showed that immediately after the reduction of working hours, workers' performance decreased more than before the reduction because they had not yet adjusted to the new hours, but gradually productivity increased significantly (Ministry of Employment and Labor, n.d.). Even if positive results don't come quickly, as in the case of KTcs, performance evaluations can help employers see how much and how performance has changed, so they can act quickly. As such, performance evaluation is necessary to identify, minimize, and stabilize productivity declines in the workplace.
The approach is to improve working environments in small and medium-sized enterprises by reducing working hours. The aim is to strengthen the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises by improving the work environment, which is poor compared to major enterprises. According to a survey by the Ministry of Employment and Labor, the number of unfilled jobs last year was at a record high of 185,000, with 93.7 percent of them coming from small and medium-sized enterprises. Small and medium-sized enterprises have plenty of jobs, but not enough workers. Even small and medium-sized enterprises in favorable geographic locations, such as metropolitan areas, are negatively viewed under the " small and medium-sized enterprises" label. To address the concentration in major enterprises, it seems necessary to create a positive perception through better conditions and environments. Effective changes can be made to the work environment of small and medium-sized enterprises through the processes of surveys, financial support, work process adjustments, and performance evaluation. Reducing working hours is an effective way to strengthen the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises and improve the quality of life of their workers directly. It is expected to have a positive impact on society as a whole, as well as help small and medium-sized enterprises increase their manpower and management stability.

title: A life-changing experience my mother gave me
text: My mother gave me a life-changing chance and experience that would shape my personality and strengthen me forever. One day, when I was 15, she asked me “If you could move to Jeju Island, would you want to move or stay in this house in Incheon?” I was so embarrassed because she never let me notice about this before. It was surprising but it was not difficult to answer that sudden suggestion. I agreed to her suggestion without giving much thought to the realistic concerns with my young mind. So, we simply moved to Jeju in a very short period. Moving to Jeju changed my life with two ways. First one is new environment of my life such as new home, new school and new friends. And second one is my changed personality. This decision and changes gave me confidence with some challenges and changes. I took on somethings that required decisions, such as completely changing and rewriting my research topic and trying out projects that took longer. Life in Jeju is many people’s dreams, but it is not easy to do in real. Someone said that our decision to move to Jeju was a difficult challenge and a decision that only enterprising people can make. However, the surprising thing is that my mother was not a challenging and enterprising person. Through her and this experience, I learned the challenge isn't only enterprising person’s thing and anyone can make some difference in their own life. I also realized that we don't have to worry too much or be afraid of the practicalities when we start or change something. I will never forget this experience that my mother gave me and led to make a difference in my life and I will make my changed personality even stronger.

title: The Unusual Day Between My Daily Life
text: There was an unusual day in my daily life because of my friend. She has been my friend since I was in middle school, but we have not seen or contacted each other since I finished my first-grade semester and transferred to another school. One day on my birthday, she suddenly sent me a message to congratulate me. It was unexpected as it was the first time we talked on message after I moved. Since then, we've stayed in touch and even made plans to meet up. The day we planned came and we were a little worried that we wouldn't recognize each other because it had been so long. Unlike my worry, I could recognize her at a glance even though she changed her hair and style. So I was quite surprised and excited to see her. At first, we went to a cafe and talked about when we were middle school students. The experience that we shared was only one year of middle school, but we were having fun as if we were back in middle school. And then, we went out to eat dinner and share each other’s experiences of a few years we have not seen. We did not go anywhere special or do something special. However, the day we met was an unusual and special memory for me. It felt special to me because despite the long time we had been out of touch, when we met again, it was not awkward at all and we felt as comfortable as before. Seeing her again made my day unusual and unexpected, like meeting someone new, but also like seeing an old friend. I felt this was novel and unforgettable moment, so it will remain in my memory for a long time.

title: New perspectives from different music genres
text: Listening to various music genres is one of the best ways to expand your mind and perspective. Pop is probably the most popular and most people's favorite genre of music. Other genres such as classical, rock, jazz, and others seem to be less popular. I've been a fan of classical and new age genres since I started learning piano when I was young. I got this musical preference because I mainly learned classical music at my piano academy, and I didn't pay much attention to other genres because of my preference for classical music. However, when I was in middle school, I was able to join the school band with curiosity and was first introduced to the rock genre. I didn't know much about electronic music, so my bandmates recommended a lot of good music to me. The music that was new to me didn't sound bad and made me curious about the genre. It was interesting that the instruments in the band's music all have their own strong characteristics, but they all blend well together. I wanted to explore more genres, so I discovered and started enjoying rock, funk, jazz, pop, and so many other genres, and expanded my musical spectrum. When I wasn't exposed to different genres, I thought what I liked was the best and didn't think to challenge and approach what other people liked. But once I did, I realized that there are so many different ways of musical expression and artistic worlds out there. Try to enjoy the new atmosphere of the music and listen closely to the sounds of the instruments that are composing it and you will realize its charm.  Now, I have a really wide variety of music interests and I enjoy discovering new and different music all the time. I don't know every genre, but I'm glad that there's still a lot of music out there for me to discover. I hope to continue to challenge and enjoy many genres in my life.

title: The Tough Reality of Camping
text: Camping is the hardest hobby because of physical toughness, high costs, and lack of comfort. First, camping is physically tiring with many works. You must set up the tent yourself and need to carry heavy gear on your own. You also must endure heat during the day and cold at night. Many camping sites are in small mountains and there is strong sunshine during the day and chilly air during the night. This is not the end, after you enjoy your camping days, you will have to take down your tent and pack up your bag again. Going camping means doing work without benefits. Second, camping costs too much. Camping requires various equipment such as a tent, foldable chairs, and a foldable table. These camping gears are generally expensive. Additionally, you need to buy a lot of groceries and other supplies. It is an expensive hobby, which makes it hard to get started. Lastly, camping is uncomfortable. Eating, sleeping, and staying outside is a very uncomfortable and tough thing to do. There are a lot of bugs and sometimes it's hard to access electricity. Sleeping and showering conditions are not convenient. I often go camping and enjoy it, but so I really know how camping is tough hobby. While camping can be a great way to connect with nature, the challenges with physical toughness, high costs, and lack of comfort make camping one of the toughest hobbies to enjoy.

title: Makeover Your Desktop: A Guide to Organizing Your Desktop
text: Cleaning up your desktop makes a more productive digital workspace and better performance. By following these steps, you can clear out unnecessary things and set up your desktop to be well-organized and efficient. The first step is to uninstall unused or old programs. You may have installed programs that you needed but rarely use, and soon you'll find that a lot of them are using up your storage space. By uninstalling these programs, you can make your desktop more pleasant, such as regaining storage space and booting up faster. The second step is to delete unneeded files. You can clean up your desktop by deleting screenshots, downloads, and anything else you've temporarily saved on it. The third step is to back up your files. When you've done a cleaning up of the unneeded files, organize them and back them up on cloud services such as Google Drive, Dropbox, or iCloud. This step will help you manage your storage space effectively and keep your files safe. The next step is to factory reset the desktop or reformat your hard drive. This is not an essential step, but it can really clean up your desktop and improve its performance. This is because simply deleting a program or file doesn't completely remove the invisible leftover data on your system such as registry entries, cache files, and system settings. After you've done reset, you can do the final step. Finally, download the files you need to save and install the latest version of the programs. You can create folders to organize these files. If you follow these steps once or twice a year regularly, you'll be able to make an efficient work environment and keep your computer performance great for a long time. Try this and feel like you just got a new computer with a new desktop environment.

title: Two Varieties of Guitars: Acoustic and Electric
text: Acoustic guitars and electric guitars have different characteristics that add to their unique musical charm. The first difference is the way of sound. Both types of guitars are played in a similar way, but they produce sound in different ways. Acoustic guitars naturally make sound through a soundbox. Electric guitars use an amplifier and pickups (pieces that receive vibrations from an guitar and turns them into electrical signals) to increase the sound with an electronic signal. The second difference is tone and genre. Similarly, both guitars can be used for a variety of musical genres, but acoustic guitars have a warmer, mellower tone. They are suited for acoustic pop, ballads, folk, country and jazz. In contrast, electric guitars have a stronger tone and can produce a wide range of sound effects and are good for rock, metal, jazz, pop and blues. The last difference is the playing environment. Acoustic guitars are played without an amplifier or additional equipment. So they are more portable and good for outdoor or small scale performance. On the other hand, electric guitars require an amplifier and effecter. They are not portable but effective for stage performances or in the studio. Thus, acoustic and electric guitars can be chosen for a variety of musical styles and playing situations thanks to their unique features and strengths. Both guitars have their own charms and offer different musical experiences.

title: Different School Life in Chinese International School and Korean Schools
text: The school life of students in Korea and China has many differences. First, there are differences in the school calendar and school events. Korean schools start the school year in March and end in February, with summer and winter breaks. On the other hand, Chinese international schools start the first semester in August, have a winter break from December to January, and a long summer vacation from June to August. The differences are also seen in school events. Chinese international schools have many different students from different nationalities, so they celebrate “International Day” with parades and food festivals. Students dress in traditional costumes and share their culture. Second, there are differences in classes and curriculum. A big difference in curriculum is the importance of history. Korean schools emphasize teaching Korean history, but Chinese international schools focus on world history and rarely teach Chinese history. There are also differences in the way that classes are organized. While Korea divides grades based on their birth year, international schools divide grades based on birthday. For example, student who born in 2005 August to 2006 July divided in same grade. In addition, classes are divided up to six levels depending on academic achievement. Students in lower-level classes may take classes below their grades, allowing for personalized learning. Third, club and sports activities are different. Clubs at Chinese international schools are usually organized by students. Especially sports clubs are very common and there are many different sports including soccer, basketball, swimming, and cheerleading. The sports clubs change from semester to semester, and students can join several sports teams at the same time to experience a variety of sports. There are also many opportunities to compete with other schools and enjoy competition and socialization. In contrast, Korean schools have a more limited selection of clubs and are often organized by teachers rather than students. Korean schools and Chinese international schools have different school calendars, classrooms, and club activities. These differences reflect the cultural background of each school.

title: Different Meanings of Gesture for English and Korean Speakers
text:
English speakers use a variety of hand gestures to convey additional meaning with their words. Gestures are an important form of nonverbal communication, but they can cause misunderstandings. The same gesture can be interpreted differently based on cultural differences.
The first one is the hand gesture asking someone to come. English speakers use the palm up and fingers bent gesture when they want to tell someone to come. On the other hand, Korean speakers use palms down and fingers bent more commonly. For Koreans, the palm up gesture may be considered rude because it is used as a command to come or to call a dog. The difference in palm direction may seem to be a very small difference, but it can cause problems in communication because they have different meanings.
The second one is the hand gesture for emphasis and quotation marks. English speakers often use the gesture of bending and unbending the index and middle fingers of both hands. It implies that a word or phrase is being used in an ironic way. However, this gesture is not commonly used in Korean culture. When I first saw this hand gesture in an American drama, I thought it was cute, as if it represents bunny ears. Like this, Koreans may not understand the meaning of this gesture at all.
The third one is the hand gesture to symbolize money. A common gesture for English speakers is rubbing thumb and index finger together. Whereas, for Korean speakers, it's common to make a circle with the thumb and index finger. Interestingly, English speakers use this circle gesture to mean “okay”, so they will think it is okay sign first rather than money. In this way, the same gesture can be used to mean completely different things, which can lead to misunderstandings.
Differences in gesture meanings between English and Korean speakers can lead to miscommunication. Learning the gestures of other countries and being respectful of cultural differences is essential for good communication. If you learn different cultural gestures and communicate with an open mind, you'll be able to reduce misunderstandings and communicate more effectively.

title: Disadvantages of Living in a Dormitory: Importance of a Different Lifestyle
text:
Many students consider living in dormitories when they enter university. Adjusting to university life can be challenging, and first-year students may choose to live in a dormitory to adapt. Living in the dormitories offers the convenience of being close to campus and is a great option for students from other regions. Although dormitories can help students to adapt to school life, they are not essential for everyone. The requirement for all first-year college students to live in school dormitories can ignore individual needs and preferences. I live with my family and commute to school by subway. I am really satisfied with this life, and it helped my school life in my first year. Each student needs to choose a lifestyle that suits them. Based on my experience with commuting, other lifestyles such as living with your family or living alone can be equally effective for a successful university life. So, I will discuss the limitations of dormitory life and why it is not necessary for students.
First, most dormitories cannot offer personal time and space for rest. Most dormitories offer one room for three or four students, and they must live in one room together. So, it is hard to get some personal time and space. Time at the dormitory cannot assure you enough rest. I once heard from my friend that she still cannot fully adapt to the school dormitory and does not feel comfortable. She said that the dormitory is mostly shared space, which makes it difficult to have time for herself. However, it is so important to rest and recharge enough for good school life and mental health. In addition, it is difficult to enjoy hobbies at the dormitory. For me, my hobbies such as playing the piano and bass guitar help me a lot to control my stress. To adapt to school life, I focused on enough rest and dealing with stress from an unfamiliar environment and lots of assignments and these worked. But it's hard to enjoy a variety of hobbies in a dormitory. Simple, quiet hobbies like knitting or reading are possible, but hobbies that make noise or require space, such as playing an instrument or exercising, are not possible. These limitations can make it difficult to manage the stress of college life and recharge energy.
Second, there's no life outside of school. While commuting to school can be a challenge because it's not as close as a dormitory, it also has its advantages. Commuting allows for more freedom to explore areas outside the school environment. Students who commute are constantly moving between campus and outside of campus and have a wide range of activities. I live in Incheon, and commuting to school in Seoul has given me a better understanding of the geography and transportation in Incheon and Seoul. I sometimes commute in different ways, so my geography sense has become useful when I go to other places. Also, it is easier to maintain a separation between school and personal life. This separation has a positive effect on your mental health, as you can come home and forget about the stresses of school for a while. On the other hand, living in a dormitory can blur the lines between school and personal time and make it difficult to relax. I've lived in a dormitory for a while in high school, despite living really close to school. The distance between home and dormitory was very close, but dormitory life was very different from home. The dormitory was still inside the school, so it didn't feel like home and comfortable at all. I realized from this experience that I need space separation from school to relax. Some people may feel comfortable living in a dormitory, but some people, like me, need space separation from life outside of school.
Last, Finally, personal preferences and personalities are important factors in the suitability of dormitory life. Strict rules and limited time for activities can be challenging for some people. Some people may struggle with the curfews and rules of the dormitory. For example, my friend was forced to choose dormitory living because she came from Jeju Island, and she had difficulty following the many rules and restrictions of the dormitory. She always wanted to have a free university life and often broke the dormitory rules. Eventually, she received penalty points a lot and was banned from the dormitory. She moved to another dormitory run by Gyeonggi Province, which was freer than the school dormitory. In addition, dormitories require you to live with a roommate, so it's important to be comfortable with living with someone. One of the reasons I didn't choose a dormitory is that I often live an irregular life. This could cause discomfort for my roommate if I were living with them. If I turn on the lights and do something when my roommate is sleeping, it would be annoying for both of us. At home, this is not a problem because I use my room alone, but it can be a problem in a shared room. The dormitory environment may be ideal for some students, but it doesn't fit everyone's preferences or personality. It's important to give students the freedom to choose the lifestyle that suits them best.
In conclusion, while dormitory living can be useful for some students, it is not the best solution for every student. The requirement to live in school dormitories may not reflect each student's individual needs and preferences. Students should be able to choose the living style that suits their needs. Flexibility should be allowed for students to choose their lifestyle. For some students, commuting or living outside of campus can provide the personal time and flexibility they need to adapt to university. These different choices are different ways students manage stress and balance their lives. This will allow universities to create a more inclusive and supportive environment for students, regardless of their lifestyle. I would like students to consider more different ways of living and find out what is most comfortable and suitable for them.

title: Can People's Ratings Become an Identity?
text:
In the Netflix series 'Black Mirror', in the episode 'Nosedive', people live based on ratings. They upload posts to their social media and receive star ratings from other people. Many aspects of everyday life, such as renting a house, renting a car, and choosing a seat on an airplane, are offered differently based on ratings. Many characters, including the main character Lacie, live a life focused on raising their ratings and ignoring their true feelings. Their ratings become their achievement and goal in life, and their ratings become their identity. In the real world, individuals are also constantly being judged by others. We are judged in various ways by various groups, such as social media, school, and work. As a result, many people define themselves based on their ratings. However, an identity based on ratings is never a healthy way to live and build self-esteem.
First, the ratings of people on social media or in society cannot measure a person's character, life, or thoughts. It's not proper to use numerical ratings or specific abilities to determine a quality of a person. Also, ratings based on people's attention or favor, such as on social media, are not a good way to value someone. In ‘Nosedive’, people rate each other based on feelings. Each person has their own life and uniqueness, including their morality, social ability, and background. However, there is no standard to measure these factors. I asked my friend for an interview and asked her how she felt about other people judging her. She does not use social media much, so she told me how she felt about being graded in school. She said that when she was in high school, she felt that the system of evaluating her assignments and grades was too partial. She also said, “The grades were written in numbers, so it felt like it was a label to me.” She said she was obsessed with her grades because she felt pressured and stressed. However, after a few years, she realized that her obsession was too weird and wanted to break it. So, she started to explore what she really wanted to do. It can be hard to stop thinking about how you're being rated, both numerical like grades and non-numerical like people's words or comments on social media. But it's important to remember that it does not fully measure or define you.
Second, other people's ratings do not reflect one's own beliefs or perceptions of oneself. As children grow up, they discover their beliefs and values through their experiences and what they learn. This shapes their identity and strengthens their respect and awareness of themselves. Identity should be made by self-reflection. However, other people's ratings miss the important elements that make up identity. I asked my friend what she thinks is the most important thing that shapes her identity. She said that her background seems to be the main factor. She was born and raised on Jeju Island, went to college in Seoul, and moved to live in Seoul. She said she still considers herself a person from Jeju and feels like an alien in Seoul. In addition, she emphasized that beliefs are also important. She said, “I want to be a person who lives happily with nature”. She is someone who cares about protecting and respecting nature but also cares about her own health and happiness. She said that people who don't know about her values, beliefs, and background feel uncomfortable or ineffective about how she lives and behaves. However, friends and family members who know her well respect her and often tell her that she is amazing. In this way, external judgment can ignore something really important about identity.
Lastly, social pressures can be caused by living based on the judgment and expectations of others. Lacie in ‘Nosedive’ tries to keep up with others' expectations to get high ratings. She might not realize that she's being pressured to act unnaturally. But as her younger brother said, her behavior and life don't seem natural at all. Another friend I interviewed told me about her own experience of feeling pressured in school. She said that in the new semester, she pretended to be a nice, calm person to get along with her classmates. She is a funny and cheerful person, but she felt that her personality was too different from the other friends. So, she tried to be more like her friends. However, she found it too hard and felt pressured, so she wanted to be herself again. “In the end, being myself was the better way,” she said, “and I felt better in school and in my relationships with my friends." These social pressures can reduce an individual's happiness and quality of life. Identities and goals created through the ratings and expectations of others are not beneficial to living for yourself.
In conclusion, the rating of others does not reflect a person's true character or the complexity of their life. The Black Mirror episode “Nosedive” clearly shows the negative impact of the rating system on a person's identity. As my friends' experiences showed, when external ratings ignore a person's values and beliefs, they can lose their identity. The pressure to live to the expectations of others can harm a person's happiness and lower their self-esteem. Life on a rating keeps us from discovering our true selves. We need to build our identity based on our own values and beliefs, not on external evaluations. A healthy life is about self-reflection and self-awareness. It should be defined by our true selves, not by ratings. We need to seek to understand ourselves fully.

title: Huge birth rate control budgets and declining birth rates: Why various financial support policies have failed to solve the problem and what more needs to be done?
text:
Do you have a desire to have children? Kyewan Cho states South Korea has invested KRW 280 trillion in a low birthrate policy over the 16 years from 2006 to 2021. Despite this large amount of money, the birth rate has been declining yearly. According to KOSIS, the total birth rate in 2023 is 0.72, and the total birth rate in the fourth quarter of last year was 0.65, according to Kyung-Rak Min.  The key point of addressing the declining birth rate is not just financial support, but what is the underlying cause of this problem? Why is the birth rate declining so much?
The survey question “Which of the following do you think is most important in your life?” examined what people value in life and whether it's more important than marriage and having children. 75% of respondents said marriage and having children are considered an important part of their life. However, only 1 respondent chose “Marriage and having children” as ‘the most’ important thing. “Marriage and having children” was chosen as the second most important, and “Career and workplace” was selected as the first most important.
These results may show that most of the respondents do not consider marriage and having children as ‘the first thing’ of their life even though they think it is an important part.
In addition, these give a supposition that excessive careerism and long working hours can negatively impact marriage and birth. What's important to focus on is that respondents are clearly considering marriage and having children and that it's not their primary consideration, but rather a second. Furthermore, those who want to get married and have children far outnumber those who don't in the survey, seven out of eight to one. This raises the question of whether other factors beyond their values are more influential in young people's decision not to get married and have children.
75% of the respondents agree working conditions, such as excessive careerism and long working hours, significantly impact low birth rates. This is related to their primary choice of Career and workplace. The reason why respondents who want to get married and have children consider Career and workplace to be the most important thing in their lives is that they believe that having a stable job and income is a necessary first step for getting married and having children. However, if excessive careerism and long working hours are making it difficult for them to have time for their lives, it is hard for them to consider marriage and having children, which are their secondary concerns. We need to improve working hours and working conditions so that they can afford to consider marriage and family.
Jin-seok Kim, a professor of social welfare at Seoul Women’s University said “We need an approach that will guarantee the quality of life for people who choose marriage and childbirth. I think the government offering various perks for people who have children is no longer a valid approach,”. Ha-yan Choi, Tae-ho Ahn, and Jong-o Park state it is necessary to improve them to ensure the quality of life for those who choose to marry and have children. Creating an environment where people can focus on their life and family is necessary. In addition, Corneliu Bente, the president of Romania's national labor law expert union, advised Korean companies to focus on work-life balance and avoid an excessive focus on careers. He was concerned that too much careerism would lead to late marriage and births. Governments and companies have to ensure work and work-life balance to allow people to consider having a family and focus on their family life more easily.
The survey respondents mention changing people's perceptions, improving birth control policy, solving housing problems and economic recovery, and government child-rearing expenses support as the first thing that needs to be done to solve South Korea's low birth rate. According to Min-Kyung Jung, South Korea's National Assembly speaker called for legislating solutions to the low birthrate and emphasized the need for a more long-term policy. South Korea has not been able to sustain a long-term policy to improve the birth rate and reduce the population. As shown, there are still a variety of issues facing South Korea, and they are linked to the low birthrate. There are also policy weaknesses, as pointed out by the speaker of South Korea's National Assembly. One of the respondents said “I believe that a world where people want to have children needs to be created first. It seems that a society where competition is natural in areas like entrance exams or employment makes people not want to have children.”.
Having children is not becoming a top priority for young people, as the survey shows that careers are prioritized over having children. But we need to make sure that work and family life are balanced, not make them a top priority. We need to improve the working environment and careerism atmosphere. In addition, government support, addressing housing and employment issues, and creating more long-term policies are also important. The continuing decline in the birth rate is not due to a single, simple cause, such as young people wanting to live alone and not wanting to get married and have children or lack of money. The causes of the problem are always complex and not simple. It is impossible to control the birth rate by completely solving all the various causes, such as personal values, social context, employment problems, housing problems, etc. However, what we need to focus on is continuing to take it one step at a time, identifying and improving the challenges and problems. We also need to make an effort to identify and understand the difficulties faced by people who want to marry and have children but are unable to do so.

title: Impact of AI: stealthy and hard-to-identify penetration
text:
"Hey ChatGPT, tell me when and how the moon was destroyed." ChatGPT didn't hesitate to answer my ridiculous question. It was quite a shock to me that it could give a detailed explanation even with untrue information. The question was intentional, so it was easy to recognize that ChatGP was lying. But would I recognize a false answer easily if I asked a question about something I didn't know or was curious about? Artificial intelligence developments have greatly impacted our lives in recent times. AI is being utilized including influencers, models, and conversational AI bots, and provides us with many benefits, such as giving us information more easily or increasing our productivity and efficiency. However, these impacts are not always positive. In particular, the spreading of misinformation and fake news occurs with conversational AI. In this editorial, I will discuss and highlight conversational AI’s negative impact: the concern of spreading misinformation with penetration and strong messaging of AI.
AI is used in so many ways and has entered our lives without us even realizing it. Because AI is still so immature, we think it's easy to recognize, but that's not always the case. I've seen videos of gamers interacting with NPCs in games with conversational AI, and I've seen AI carry on conversations as if it were a real person and speak very fluently. I was amazed at the conversational skills of the NPCs, and if I had met them on social media or other media instead of in-game, I could almost believe I was talking to a real person. According to Brandi Wampler from <Notre Dame News>, Researchers at the University of Notre Dame conducted a study using AI bots based on large language models and 58% of participants were unable to identify the AI. Also, Callum Jones from <UNILAD> states AI influencer Emily is being asked to have dates by celebrities. Research on the difficulty of identifying AI bots on social media shows how stealthily and deeply AI can enter our lives. This can be a problem because we can indiscreetly accept information without knowing whether it is coming from an AI or a real person.
AI can also be used to spread misinformation. According to <NGNMagazine>, Tomo Lazovich expressed concern about spreading misinformation and unreliable information. There are examples of AI spreading misinformation. In the United States, a 30-year veteran lawyer was tricked by ‘ChatGPT’ into writing an argument to the court citing "false precedents" created by ChatGPT. This is also an example of the hallucinations mentioned earlier. <The New York Times> reported that at least six of the cases he cited were false. He said he believed them because ChatGPT responded that they were real cases and that he could find them in other legal databases. I have felt AI makes us believe it through its conversational skill, trusting tone, and plausible words, just as AI tricked the lawyer. AI can easily spread and access misinformation like this, and it's hard for us to identify it.
AI is known for its potential to be used effectively in marketing and advertising because it can spread a strong message easily and fast. Cesareo Contreras from <NGNMagazine> explains AI influencers have the advantage of effective marketing through spreading strong messaging. However, the pervasiveness and accessibility of AI is causing concern. This is because powerful messaging, pervasiveness, and accessibility of AI are dangerous when it's used to spread misinformation, whether intentionally or not. Have you ever experienced hallucinations with ChatGPT? Hallucinations are a phenomenon in which an AI says information that isn't actually there or isn't true as if it were. This makes the AI's statements seem so plausible that you believe them regardless of whether they are true or not. Paul Brenner, a faculty member and director of the Center for Research Computing at Notre Dame and senior author of the study states the impact of conversational bots’ information is more powerful than information from abstract comments or references. Moreover, he comments these AI bots have a position of strength to receive misinformation because of the difficulty of identifying. This shows how the pervasiveness and accessibility of AI can influence us strongly and can be a danger if not used properly.
To sum up, AI has brought many changes to our lives, but we should be aware of its negative impacts. They can penetrate various media covertly and spread information more widely because they are difficult to identify. Through this, they can influence us powerfully and convey information or messages strongly and effectively. This is a huge advantage when used positively, but a huge risk when abused to spread fake news, incite, etc. Strong regulations and punishments are needed to prevent the abuse of AI to manipulate or incite public opinion and spread fake news. In addition, we need to be concerned about the danger of exposing misinformation and unreliable information. I want to emphasize that you should be aware of these issues and carefully consider the use of AI. When we get information from various sources, including social media, we should always be suspicious and double-check the facts rather than immediately believing. Through this, I hope that we can wisely take advantage of the usefulness and convenience of AI to enrich our lives.
